title: Info Edge (India) Ltd - 532777 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Info Edge Q2 FY27: standalone billings up 13% YoY, revenue up 13% to Rs.842 crore, operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore; CEO Hitesh Oberoi steps down Dec 2.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 standalone billings grew 13% and revenue 13% to Rs.842 crore, with operating profit up 30% to Rs.347 crore and operating PBT margin of 41% (up 541 bps). Management said renewal timing shifted billings between Q1 and Q2, so H1 (billings +14%, revenue +12%) is the better read, with underlying growth guided at about 14-15%. Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi announced he will step down as MD and CEO at close of business on December 2, with Sanjeev Bikhchandani becoming Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from December 3; Oberoi stays on the board subject to shareholder approval. Management said AI-first products now run at a Rs.240 crore annualised rate, and 99acres reached near-breakeven operating losses with positive cash generation.

segments.name: Recruitment (Naukri)
segments.commentary: Q2 billings +13%, revenue +13%, operating profit +20% at 59% operating PBT margin; H1 billings +15%. Q2 IT/Tech/BPM billings +3%, GCCs +7%, other sectors +18%, consultants +7%. Naukri 360 billings +37%; Job Hai billings +86%; NaukriGulf +9% at about 36% margin.

segments.name: Real Estate (99acres)
segments.commentary: Billings +21% YoY in Q2 (up from 17% in Q1), revenue +17%. Operating loss cut 93% from Rs.23 crore to under Rs.2 crore; operating cash flow Rs.22 crore vs Rs.2 crore a year ago. Marketing spend down about 13% YoY while enquiries grew 33%.

segments.name: Matchmaking (Jeevansathi, Aisle)
segments.commentary: Billings +23% in Q2 (Jeevansathi +18%, Aisle +40%). Segment near breakeven at operating PBT; Jeevansathi operating profit Rs.2 crore, Aisle operating loss Rs.3 crore. Segment cash generation Rs.3 crore vs cash loss Rs.2 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Education (Shiksha)
segments.commentary: Billings -27% and revenue -9% in Q2; near breakeven at operating PBT with cash loss of Rs.16 crore. AI-driven search changes cut referral traffic; company is pivoting to domestic counselling with AI voice bots and widening Study Abroad destinations (UK, UAE, continental Europe).

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Portfolio of about 135 companies across AI, deeptech and consumer tech, with about Rs.5,000 crore invested via balance sheet and AIFs.

guidance_outlook: Management views underlying business growth at about 14-15% and is setting sales team targets on that basis.

Target of 100% growth in Job Hai billings this year; Job Hai burn about Rs.45 crore a year, taking about 2-3% off overall Naukri margin; breakeven estimated at Rs.100-125 crore topline, possibly taking a couple of years (later framed as Rs.120-130 crore).
99acres expected to generate positive operating cash for FY27 and to see operating leverage progressively through the rest of FY27; aims for further traffic and revenue share gains in H2.
Jeevansathi billing growth expected to accelerate in H2; Aisle expected to continue high growth.
Management said margins are not the current focus; it aims to keep sales growing above 10% YoY, and does not expect margins to decline.
capex_capacity: Management continues to step up investment in AI infrastructure, talent and tools; Job Hai investment levels broadly unchanged in the quarter.
Job Hai and 99acres marketing spend managed for efficiency; 99Shorts being taken beyond NCR to more cities.
New Projects opportunity estimated at about Rs.6,000 crore across digital and non-digital spend; expansion is a strategic priority through content, product and client delivery.
demand_pricing: AI and data products now a high single-digit share of Recruitment topline; annualised run rate about Rs.240 crore (Q2 AI-first revenue about Rs.60 crore x4). AI-Rex had little revenue in Q1 and scaled sharply in Q2.
AI-Rex: about 2,000 accounts using it vs a potential base of about 40,000 large clients; rate card Rs.3,500 per mandate for companies and Rs.2,500 for consultants. Talent Pulse used by 750 companies.
Clients buying AI offerings paid on average 10-15% more than non-buyers, per management.
Consultant revenue growth slowed to 5% in H1 (2-3% excluding AI-Rex); IT services hiring remains mostly replacement-driven.
Paid subscribers reached 2.7% of Naukri monthly active users vs 1.3% in January 2025.
99acres: about 50% revenue share in core categories per management; competitor revenue reportedly declined; Housing sold to Aurum, which targets breakeven in 4-5 quarters.
Naukri unique paying customers flat YoY at 46,000 (down from 49,000 QoQ), as the company reworked low-ticket e-commerce offers.

qa_highlights.question: Will Sanjeev be a full-time CEO or a stopgap, and what changes are expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjeev said no decision has been taken on the long-term structure; he will consult the NRC, Hitesh remains available for counsel, and no hiring decision has been made.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q2 billings growth of 13% the new normal after Q1's 17.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said timing shifts are behind the swing; Q1 was about 14-15% underlying and business is growing about 14-15%. Revenue is recognised over 12 months, so renewal timing defers into later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will AI-Rex lift margins, and what is the steady-state margin?
qa_highlights.answer: AI products are high gross margin, but the GTM is penetration-first over about 24 months; management declined to give a steady-state margin and said margins should not fall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AI revenue run rate additive, and is pricing bundled?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs.240 crore is Q2 revenue x4; AI-first products contributed about Rs.60 crore in Q2 and are largely additive, with prior-year AI revenue mainly Talent Pulse and jobseeker services. Products are priced separately on rate cards but often sold as a negotiated bundle.

qa_highlights.question: Why did unique customers stay flat at 46,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said small low-ticket e-commerce buyers were pruned and offers repriced higher; e-commerce revenue is up even though buying customers fell.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Job Hai margin drag and breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Job Hai burn about Rs.45 crore a year, 2-3% of Naukri margin; breakeven at Rs.100-125 crore topline, possibly over a couple of years.

qa_highlights.question: Is IT and GCC growth sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: IT hiring is mostly replacement-led and Naukri's share is at risk in consultants; GCC growth in the teens is driven by mid-size and small GCCs, with larger GCCs more exposed to US layoffs.

risks_watch: CEO transition: Hitesh Oberoi leaves full-time role Dec 2; Sanjeev Bikhchandani (age 63) becomes Group CEO Dec 3 with no successor or CBO named; CBO roles at 99acres and other units are vacant or unclear, and Pawan left Naukri a few months ago.
Billings timing noise from renewal shifts; Q3 billings may swing again.
Shiksha billings -27% and cash losses of Rs.16 crore in Q2 while the business model pivots.
Consultant channel slowdown (H1 revenue growth 5%) as IT services firms cut costlier channels.
AI revenue durability: 2,000 AI-Rex accounts trying the product; management said the run-rate depends on these customers renewing next year.
Job Hai and Naukri 360 investment continues to dilute margins; NaukriGulf recovery depends on regional conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating metrics, 99acres and AI traction, but cautious on the Q2 billings slowdown, which management attributed to renewal timing. Evasive on succession details, with no named successor or CBO plan. Hitesh Oberoi framed the CEO exit as a planned handover to a strong internal team.
key_quotes: Excluding Shiksha, standalone billings grew over 14% in Q2 and about 16% in H1, against reported growth of 13% and 14%, respectively.
Our goal for the next, I would say, maybe 24 months is going to be to drive penetration, to get as many customers to use AI-Rex as possible, and then to get them to adopt it, use it and then renew.
Margins are not really our focus right now. It's about getting more sales, it's about getting more users, more clients, it's about getting adoption going.
We are hiring business, not the firing business.

growth.why: Management guides underlying growth of about 14-15% (sales to keep growing above 10%), backed by AI product run-rate of about Rs.240 crore, Job Hai targeting 100% billings growth and 2,000 AI-Rex accounts, but no specific capacity or contracted orders are quantified, and Shiksha billings fell 27%.

roles: Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO (Sanjeev Bikhchandani, from Dec 3)
mgmt.note: Co-promoter Hitesh Oberoi steps down as MD and CEO effective close of Dec 2; Sanjeev Bikhchandani takes over as Executive Vice Chairman, MD and Group CEO from Dec 3, with an AI-led growth agenda but no explicit new capacity.
initiatives: AI-first products (AI-Rex, Talent Pulse) scaling; AI-Rex at about 2,000 accounts vs ~40,000 potential
Job Hai billings growth target of 100% in FY27
99acres to reach positive operating cash in FY27 and operating leverage through H2
Jeevansathi billing acceleration in H2; Aisle high growth
